item.title: 14×6″ Mercedes-Benz Bundt Alloy Wheels by Fuchs at No Reserve
item.description: These 14×6.5″ Bundt alloy wheels were produced by Fuchs for use on Mercedes-Benz models. The forged wheels are painted silver, retain center caps, and were refinished in preparation for the sale. This set of forged Bundt wheels is now offered by 1600veloce, a Local Partner, at no reserve in North Salem, New York.

item.title: 2005 Dodge Ram SRT-10 Quad Cab
item.description: This 2005 Dodge Ram SRT-10 Quad Cab pickup has remained registered in Washington since new and has 59k miles after the current owner's purchase in 2011. Powered by a Viper-sourced 8.3-liter V10 linked with a four-speed automatic transmission and a limited-slip differential, the truck is finished in black over Medium Slate Gray leather and suede. Equipment includes a body-color SnugTop bed topper, polished 22" alloy wheels, power-adjustable bolstered bucket seats, air conditioning, cruise control

item.title: 1938 LaSalle Series 38-50 Damascus Hearse by S&S
item.description: This 1938 LaSalle Series 38-50 features Damascus hearse coachwork and interior appointments by the Sayers & Scovill Company of Cincinnati, Ohio. It was reportedly used for 57 years by a funeral home in Oklahoma before it was purchased by the seller in 2017 and relocated to New Jersey. item.title: 1994 Chevrolet Corvette Convertible Widebody at No Reserve
item.description: This 1994 Chevrolet Corvette convertible is powered by a 5.7-liter LT1 V8 paired with a four-speed automatic transmission, both of which were overhauled in 2013 and 2008, respectively. It was acquired by the seller in 2025, and subsequent work consisted of installing an ACI Stalker widebody kit, a rear spoiler, a vented hood, and C8-sourced 19" and 20" wheels and repainting the car in red pearl. item.title: 8k-Mile 2004 Aston Martin V12 Vanquish
item.description: This 2004 Aston Martin V12 Vanquish is one of 2,589 examples built between 2001 and 2007, and it is finished in gray over brown leather. The car has under 8k miles following history in New York and Florida, and it is powered by a 5.9-liter V12 linked to an electro-hydraulically operated six-speed automated transmission and a limited-slip differential. Equipment includes a premium sound system, a quilted Alcantara headliner, gray carpets, 19" seven-spoke wheels, heated power-adjustable front seat

item.title: Ford GT Concept Static Display Vehicle
item.description: This 2002 Ford GT Concept display model is a non-drivable fiberglass styling buck that was constructed by Special Projects Inc. of Plymouth, Michigan, for Ford’s "Living Legends" studio. Identified as chassis GT1147, the model was unveiled at the 2002 North American International Auto Show in Detroit to gauge public interest in a revival of the GT40. Following its promotional duties, the car was transferred from Ford to Safir GT40 Spares, Ltd., and later spent over 15 years with Russ Milne Ford

item.title: 1956 Austin-Healey 100 BN2 Roadster
item.description: This 1956 Austin-Healey 100 BN2 roadster was ordered new by an officer of the United States Army stationed near Düsseldorf, Germany. item.title: This Week’s Weird and Wonderful—January 23, 2026
item.description: If you're one of the millions out there hunkering down for a cold weekend, you're probably pondering how best to spend your time indoors. item.title: 1975 Maserati Merak at No Reserve
item.description: This 1975 Maserati Merak is one of 830 examples produced between 1972 and 1975, and it is said to have been stored in a collection since being sold on BaT in August 2023. Finished in red over black upholstery, the car is powered by a 3.0-liter V6 mated to a five-speed manual transaxle.
